Read a resistor's first two color bands as a two-digit number, ignoring any band after them.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/resistor-color-duo) (MIT). Listed under [Encoding & Ciphers](/examples/?subject=encoding-and-ciphers).

```nomi-run
// FILE: resistor_color_duo.nomi
//# The two-digit value a resistor's first two color bands give.

/// A band color, in value order: black is 0 and white is 9.
pub enum Color {
    Black
    Brown
    Red
    Orange
    Yellow
    Green
    Blue
    Violet
    Grey
    White
}

/// The value the first two bands read as digits give, ignoring any band
/// after them, or `None` when there are fewer than two bands.
pub fn value(bands: List<Color>) -> Maybe<Int> {
    case bands {
        [first, second, .._] -> Some(digit(first) * 10 + digit(second))
        _ -> None
    }
}

fn digit(color: Color) -> Int {
    case color {
        .Black -> 0
        .Brown -> 1
        .Red -> 2
        .Orange -> 3
        .Yellow -> 4
        .Green -> 5
        .Blue -> 6
        .Violet -> 7
        .Grey -> 8
        .White -> 9
    }
}

// FILE: resistor_color_duo_test.nomi
import {
    resistor_color_duo
    resistor_color_duo.Color
}

test "value" {
    cases = [
        #("Brown and black", [Color.Brown, .Black], 10),
        #("Blue and grey", [.Blue, .Grey], 68),
        #("Yellow and violet", [.Yellow, .Violet], 47),
        #("White and red", [.White, .Red], 92),
        #("Orange and orange", [.Orange, .Orange], 33),
        #("Ignore additional colors", [.Green, .Brown, .Orange], 51),
        #("Black and brown, one-digit", [.Black, .Brown], 1),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, bands, expected), description {
        assert resistor_color_duo.value(bands) == Some(expected)
    }
}

// Not a canonical case: the exercise always gives at least two bands.
test "fewer than two bands have no value" {
    assert resistor_color_duo.value([Color.Brown]) == None
}
```

## How it's written

- `value` takes the bands as a `List<Color>`, since one canonical case passes three, and matches `[first, second, .._]`.
- Fewer than two bands answer `None`, so `value` returns `Maybe<Int>`. The canonical data never gives fewer; the test file adds one such case, marked as not canonical. A band list is data the caller may have read from anywhere, so a missing band is an answer rather than a trap (style §28).
- The `Color` enum and its `digit` table are repeated from resistor-color: each exercise stands alone.
- The table qualifies only the first row's first color (`[Color.Brown, .Black]`); every later bare variant, in its own row's list, takes that enum.
